questions.prompt: OpenAI's admin setup guide gives a way to test a restriction before users rely on it. What is it?

options.text: Ask users after a month whether they noticed any blocked actions.
options.explanation: That checks too late. The guide says to test before users rely on it.

options.text: Read the policy text again, since a clear policy always works as written.
options.explanation: Reading is not testing. The guide says to try the actions.

options.text: Test one action the policy should allow and one action it should block.
options.explanation: Right. The guide says to resolve the issue before users rely on a restriction that does not work.

questions.prompt: At what levels does OpenAI's rate limits page say limits are defined?

options.text: For each user, so every person gets a limit of their own.
options.explanation: The page says the opposite: not at user level.

options.text: At the organization and project levels, not at user level.
options.explanation: Right. A team that needs a per-user cap must use another control.

options.text: Only for the whole company, with no limits for projects.
options.explanation: The page names the project level as well.

questions.prompt: Anthropic's workspaces page names one workspace that supports per-user monthly spend limits. Which one?

options.text: The Default Workspace, which every organization has.
options.explanation: The page says you can't set limits on the Default Workspace.
Right. The page says it is the only workspace that supports per-user monthly spend limits.

options.text: Any new workspace an admin creates.
options.explanation: New workspaces have workspace limits, but not per-user monthly limits.
